title: Burst heap playback lab notes — Aug 20 2026
body:
Purpose / context:
We ran a focused playback of the July 30 production spike trace to reproduce a short-lived heap surge that coincided with 95p latency doubling. The goal was not only to reproduce but to produce a set of small, actionable experiments we can run in CI and on a dedicated lab cluster next week.

Attendees:
- Ayesha (owner)
- Miguel (profiling + infra)
- Jenna (runtime)
- Tomislav (observability)
- Notes: short drop-in from Farah in the middle.

High-level summary of what we saw:
- Replayed 10k requests sampled from the prod spike windows (seq len distribution preserved). Heap usage trends: stable baseline then a ~250MB step-up over ~30s during sustained mixed-length requests. The step correlated with a cluster of requests that used streaming + tool-calling paths.
- 95p latency increased from 180ms -> 380ms during the step. 50p unaffected.
- GC pause metric (measured via jemalloc stats exported by our sidecar) showed small increases but not long stop-the-world pauses.
- KV prefix cache hit-rate dropped by ~12% during the same window (suspected eviction pressure).
- OOM or crashes not observed in this run — ephemeral, but latency impact is customer-visible.

Observed artifacts (raw):
- perf profile: s3://bench-archive/2026-08/heap-playback/profiles/trace-aug20.tar.gz
- flamegraph: s3://bench-archive/.../fg-aug20.html
- heap snapshots: s3://bench-archive/.../heap-aug20-1.snap (link in LIN-3421)

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Buffer accumulation in streaming path: streaming responses allocate transient buffers which, under certain request interleavings, are held until commit and cause working set growth.
2) Cache-churn amplification: simultaneous cache misses cause many parallel decode allocations and temporary retention of KV entries until later eviction windows.
3) Native-slab fragmentation (observed in heap snapshots): some large allocations moved to the native allocator leading to fragmentation-induced higher RSS even though live set isn't larger.
4) Delayed cleanup due to callback chaining in tool-calling paths: callbacks store closures referencing large transient slices.

Quick evidence mapping:
- Buffer accumulation: flamegraph shows heavy allocation in io/stream_writer.go:Write and in encoding/stream_codec.Encode path during the step.
- Cache-churn: correlation between low prefix cache hit-rate and increase in allocations in model/decoder.go.
- Slab fragmentation: heap snapshot meta shows increased native alloc count during the step; also stomps of large mmap regions.
- Callback chaining: trace spans show several nested function closures alive between request start and background commit.

Planned experiments (short, to run in parallel if possible):
A) Re-run playback with streaming turned off (disable chunked responses) to see if heap spike disappears. (owner: Jenna)
B) Turn off prefix cache for the run (or pin cache size) to measure effect on miss amplification. (owner: Miguel)
C) Run with jemalloc tunables changed (decay settings) to test fragmentation hypothesis. (owner: Tomislav)
D) Add lightweight heap-profiler sampling (pprof heap every 10s) and a short-lived allocations-only tracing. (owner: Ayesha)
E) Run playback with reduced concurrency / increased batching to test whether interleaving is the trigger (owner: Miguel/Jenna).

Success criteria for each experiment:
- Heap spike magnitude reduced by >= 50% OR 95p latency improvement >= 30% compared to baseline replay.
- Able to reproduce reliably in lab (>=3/5 runs show same pattern) for a hypothesis to be considered plausible.

Short-term mitigation ideas (if customer impact increases):
- Auto-fallback to non-streaming response for customers on Dedicated until we have a fix (risk: UX impact).
- Aggressive prefix-cache TTL reduction during sustained high-mix windows.
- Emergency canary rollback of recent streaming change if it reproduces on feature branch.

Commands / instrumentation notes (copyable):
- Start replay (local lab): ./tools/replay --trace s3://bench-archive/2026-08/trace-0730.json --preserve-seq-dist --concurrency 40 --duration 15m
- Enable heap pprof endpoint: export ENABLE_PPROF=1 && ./start-runtime --pprof-port 6060
- jemalloc stats collection: curl http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep jemalloc > /tmp/jemo.txt

Open action items (owners + due):
- Ayesha: add allocations-only tracing and wire up pprof upload to s3 for the next 2 replays (due 2026-08-22).
- Jenna: run experiment A and paste flamegraphs (due 2026-08-23).
- Miguel: run experiments B and E on lab cluster 3 (due 2026-08-23).
- Tomislav: test jemalloc tunables (experiment C) and report memory RSS + fragmentation numbers (due 2026-08-24).
- Observability: add a lightweight synthetic that exercises streaming + tool-calls in staging to catch this earlier (owner: Tomislav, due 2026-09-01).

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- We should capture a lightweight request-id map to trace which client-level request leads to retained allocations (maybe correlate with tokenization spikes).
- Consider adding a small finalizer or explicit zeroing in the streaming buffer pool to reduce lifetime if GC behavior is delaying reclamation.
- If native fragmentation is confirmed, consider a short-term process restart policy on nodes that exceed a heap delta threshold; graceful drain then restart.

Meeting follow-up / next sync:
- Quick async updates in LIN-3421; we plan a short sync Friday 2026-08-27 if experiments produce divergent outcomes earlier.
- If one hypothesis clearly wins, schedule a design + PR branch review session to land the fix (owner depends on hypothesis).

Appendix (raw numbers from baseline replay):
- baseline RSS median: 1.8GB
- spike RSS peak: 2.06GB (delta 260MB)
- allocation rate increase during step: +48%
- prefix cache hit-rate baseline: 78% -> 66% during step

End notes: rough doc — expecting more raw artifacts added to LIN-3421 and s3 links. This is intentionally informal: leave TODO comments in the PRs instead of over-polishing here.

-- Ayesha
